alex: Heads-up — we started seeing a flake in the Android SDK tests: after a few dozen streaming calls the client hangs and subsequent requests never start. Repro on Pixel 5 emulator + Android 12. Suspect connection pool exhaustion or an okhttp retry interplay.

maria: Ugh. Any logs? stacktrace? Is it only on gRPC-like streaming or regular REST?

alex: Regular Retrofit POSTs (multipart + json) to our hosted inference endpoint. Logs show threads blocked on okhttp3.internal.connection.RealCall.getResponseWithInterceptorChain, then queued on the dispatcher. No 4xx/5xx in server. Attached a short stack dump: 

alex: ```
Thread-24 waiting at okhttp3.internal.connection.Transmitter.exchange
  at okhttp3.internal.connection.Exchange.acquireConnection(Exchange.kt:...)
  at okhttp3.internal.connection.Transmitter.newExchange(Transmitter.kt:...)
  at okhttp3.internal.connection.RealCall.getResponseWithInterceptorChain(RealCall.kt:...)
  ...
```

cheng: I ran into similar once — often caused by interceptor/Authenticator ordering + retryOnConnectionFailure. If an Authenticator triggers synchronous token refresh that blocks and then the retry path creates new calls, you can starve the dispatcher if maxRequests is low. Also HTTP/2 multiplexing + connection shutdown races can leak streams. Which okhttp version?

alex: Using okhttp 4.11.0, Retrofit 2.9, our SDK default Client is basically "new OkHttpClient.Builder().retryOnConnectionFailure(true).build()". Dispatcher is default (64/5?). Android apps usually have low concurrency but this is in CI with many parallel SDK clients.

jamie: Two quick thoughts: (1) Authenticator vs Interceptor — Authenticator runs on 401/407 at the network layer and can re-issue calls; if it does a blocking refresh that creates another Retrofit call you can end up with recursion / dispatcher queuing. Try doing token refresh outside the Authenticator (e.g., use an async refresh + suspend/resume) or guard with a single-flight. (2) retryOnConnectionFailure(true) will retry on some socket failures and can re-enqueue, doubling in-flight attempts for the same logical request.

maria: Can you paste the client config? Also what's dispatcher.maxRequests and maxRequestsPerHost in CI? If maxRequests is low and many retries happen you'll hit the queue size.

alex: client config snippet: ```java
OkHttpClient ok = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS) // streaming responses
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .build();
```
CI runner sets many clients in parallel (we spawn 50) — default dispatcher is 64 so should be okay but still seeing blocks.

cheng: Another angle — connection pool keepalive on Android can behave oddly when you mix HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 endpoints or when server closes connection but client reuses it. There were known bugs where idle connections weren't evicted properly on older Android TLS stacks. Workaround: configure ConnectionPool with an evictor or reduce keepAliveSeconds. Example: `new ConnectionPool(5, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` or periodically call connectionPool.evictAll() in tests.

jamie: For the SDK default, we should tighten defaults to be safer on mobile: lower maxRequestsPerHost, enable a short connection pool keepalive, and provide a documented guidance to set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for long-lived streaming workloads. Also avoid doing token refresh inside Authenticator synchronously — instead return null from Authenticator and surface auth failure upstream so caller can refresh then retry.

alex: Agreed. I'll open a small PR to change SDK default client to: `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)`, `new ConnectionPool(8, 15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`, and set `dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost(16)`. Will also add a warn in docs about Authenticator usage.

maria: Can we also add a sample snippet to the Android quickstart showing how to wire a single-flight token refresher (AtomicReference + suspend)? New users keep copying the naive Authenticator pattern.

cheng: One more practical test: try setting `client.connectionPool().evictAll()` between tests to see if tests recover. If that fixes it, it's definitely a pool reuse issue. Also try `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` to see if the hang goes away — that will tell us if retries are compounding the backlog.

alex: Running a quick experiment now in CI with retry disabled + pool keepalive=15s. Will report back in ~10m.

Root cause: our example Authenticator does a blocking Retrofit call to refresh token which can spawn more calls when dispatcher is saturated.
